goal: Add KML export to msfslogger in three scopes: one flight, an arbitrary user-picked set of flights, and a whole trip. Server side, a new pure module src/kmlExport.ts turns flight rows plus their flight_points into a KML 2.2 document (no ./db import, no Puppeteer, no new dependency), and src/server.ts gains GET /api/flights/:id/export.kml, GET /api/trips/:id/export.kml and a new POST endpoint that takes a JSON list of flight ids — all registered above the SPA catch-all. Client side, an 'Export KML' button appears beside 'Export PDF' on FlightDetail and TripDetail, and an 'Export KML' action joins Home's multi-select toolbar, all driven through one generalised download helper in client/src/utils/api.ts. The generator is covered by Vitest and by a ts-node inspector; nothing about the existing PDF export, page layouts or Home selection behaviour changes beyond the added entry points.
frozen_decisions: USER, verbatim: "Add kml exports, for individual flights, a set of flights or the whole trip."

PROJECT STANDING (.claude/ENVIRONMENT.md, CLAUDE.md): never stop, restart, rebuild over or reconfigure the user's server on port 3000, and never write to the live flights.db. Every server-based check runs on another port against a copy of the database, and is shut down when the task ends.

PROJECT STANDING (.claude/ENVIRONMENT.md): every node/npm/npx/ts-node command is prefixed with `export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"; . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"; nvm use 20` — the default node on this machine is v26 and better-sqlite3 will not load under it.

PLANNER, to keep parallel tasks' file ownership disjoint (Designer may not overturn silently; if the design needs either of these, it must say so explicitly in design.md §9 so the Orchestrator can re-scope the affected task): src/types.ts is NOT edited by this run — every new type (generator inputs, options, request payload) lives in src/kmlExport.ts and is imported from there; src/db.ts is NOT edited by this run — the flight-set export composes existing getFlightById() per id rather than adding a bulk query.

PLANNER: no new runtime or dev dependency. fast-xml-parser ^5.11.1 is already a dependency (used by src/lnmpln.ts); its XMLValidator is the well-formedness oracle in tests and in the inspector. Packaging, Dockerfile and puppeteer setup are therefore untouched.
sequencing_rationale: Design first, and gated by a reviewer, because the flight-set endpoint has no URL-shape precedent in this codebase (intake: closest is POST /api/flights/combine, which takes exactly two ids) and because the KML document structure — LineString vs gx:Track, one file with folders vs otherwise, what metadata rides in each Placemark, feet-to-metres and altitudeMode — is a contract that three later tasks all encode. Getting it wrong after implementation costs a rework of the module, the routes, the tests and the client.

The escape hatch ships before the automation it protects: phase 2 delivers URLs a user can paste or curl (and a ts-node inspector that needs no server at all) before phase 3 puts buttons on them. If the client wiring is delayed or reverted, the feature is still usable.

The risky part is isolated as a pure module with its own CLI inspector, per the project's established pattern (src/geo.ts, src/lnmpln.ts): rows in, KML string out, no ./db import. That makes the format falsifiable in Vitest and against real flights without a server, which matters because no KML viewer exists in this environment and 'opens in Google Earth' cannot be checked directly.

File ownership is assigned so that the only two tasks that can run at once in phase 2 — routes (src/server.ts) and unit tests (tests/kmlExport.test.ts) — cannot collide, and so that src/types.ts and src/db.ts, which both would otherwise be contested, are simply out of scope.

All four client surfaces are one task, not four: client/src/utils/api.ts must grow a POST-capable download helper (today downloadPdf is GET+query-params only, api.ts:20-50) and all three pages call it, so splitting them would put three dispatchers in the same file.

Every phase ends in a reviewer, and the first task of each phase depends on the previous phase's reviewer, so the server task and the client task can never be in flight at the same time as each other's dependencies.
Docs and the end-to-end build sweep are last, because the README must describe endpoints and buttons that already exist, and because a build sweep before the client lands proves nothing.

Scratch verification is fiddly in this repo and every task that needs it is given the recipe verbatim: src/db.ts:9 fixes the database path from process.cwd() at module load and src/server.ts:108,788 resolve client/dist the same way, so a scratch instance is a scratch *working directory* holding a DB copy with dist/client/node_modules symlinked in — there is no path or env-var override to pass. src/inspect-legmatch.ts:404-414 already documents the equivalent chdir-before-require trick for inspectors, and src/inspect-kml.ts follows it.

tasks.title: Design and freeze the KML export contract
tasks.goal: Write .claude/runs/2026-09-09-kml-export/design.md freezing every decision the implementation tasks would otherwise have to invent. Use exactly this section numbering, because later tasks cite it by number: §1 Goal and non-goals. §2 Route contracts — §2.1 GET /api/flights/:id/export.kml, §2.2 GET /api/trips/:id/export.kml, §2.3 the flight-set endpoint (method, path, request body schema, id-count cap, duplicate/unknown/out-of-order id handling, and why this shape over the alternatives — the intake's suggested direction is POST with a JSON body of ids following POST /api/flights/combine at src/server.ts:163-201, but you own the call), §2.4 status codes and error body shape for every failure mode. §3 Response headers and filename conventions — Content-Type, Content-Length, Content-Disposition, the filename pattern for each of the three scopes (mirror flightExportFilename()/slugify()/dateStamp() at src/server.ts:53-65; note that the set export has no natural name), and the header-injection sanitising rule sendPdf() already applies (src/server.ts:67-73). §4 KML document structure — §4.1 LineString vs gx:Track (and if gx:Track, the gx namespace declaration and <when> element format), §4.2 how the three scopes map onto Document/Folder/Placemark, §4.3 what metadata goes in each Placemark name and description and where it comes from (Flight fields: departure_icao, arrival_icao, aircraft, start_time, end_time, duration_sec, distance_nm, max_altitude_ft — see src/types.ts:27-53), §4.4 styles (line colour/width; whether flights in a set/trip are colour-cycled), §4.5 coordinate encoding — lon,lat,alt order, altitude_ft to metres conversion, decimal precision, altitudeMode, and whether tessellate/extrude are set, §4.6 XML escaping rule for every interpolated string, §4.7 whether long tracks are decimated and at what threshold (flights in this DB can carry thousands of flight_points rows). §5 Module API — the exported function signatures of src/kmlExport.ts and the structural input types it declares (it must compile without importing ./db; FlightWithPoints/FlightPoint from src/types.ts are type-only and may be imported, or mirrored structurally — state which), plus the src/inspect-kml.ts CLI argument surface. §6 Edge cases — flight with zero points, flight with one point, null departure_icao/arrival_icao/aircraft (combined flights have no ICAOs), null end_time (in-progress flight), unknown or non-numeric ids, empty id array, id list over the cap. §7 Client contract — the generalised signature of the download helper in client/src/utils/api.ts (it must keep every existing downloadPdf call site compiling, or state the exact call-site edits), the button copy and disabled/pending states on FlightDetail, TripDetail and the Home toolbar, and what the Home toolbar does with 0 selected. §8 Verification plan — the concrete commands each later task runs. §9 Open questions and anything this design needed from src/types.ts or src/db.ts that the planner's frozen constraint forbids. Read the intake first; it already surveyed the codebase, so do not re-survey — only open files it did not cover.
